title: Introduce lazy-schema stubs and incremental parse helpers for Python SDK streaming responses
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Design and implement a lightweight "lazy-schema stubs" system for the Python SDK that enables low-latency streaming consumers to access only the fields they need without fully hydrating heavy Pydantic/dataclass models. Goal: improve first-byte and incremental latency for streaming responses, reduce GC and memory churn for large response streams, and provide clear ergonomics for users who need partial fields during stream consumption.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a documented LazyStub base that can be constructed from a streaming JSON chunk boundary and exposes attribute accessors which parse on-demand
Integrate with existing streaming iterator API such that streaming consumers can choose full hydration (Pydantic/dataclass) or lazy stubs per-request
Performance: reduce median first-field access latency for streaming generation by >= 35% on benchmark prompt set compared to baseline full hydration
Memory: peak resident memory during large-batch stream replay reduced by >= 25% on our perf harness
Backward compatible: existing examples that call .to_model() to get a fully validated model should still work and preserve validation semantics
Ship unit and integration tests covering partial access, edge-case missing fields, malformed chunk boundaries, and retry scenarios
implementation_notes: Design: LazyStub stores raw JSON bytes slice and a small parse index mapping for top-level keys; attribute access triggers a fast parse of just that key using orjson / rapidjson bindings
Hydration paths: implement LazyStub.to_pydantic() and .to_dataclass() helpers which perform full validation/hydration when requested
Streaming API changes: add optional 'response_schema_mode' param to stream endpoints: 'eager' (current), 'lazy', 'hybrid'
Retries: ensure stub preserves offsets and can be re-parsed after an idempotent retry; include explicit checkpoint serialization to support durable client-side retry across process restarts
Error handling: attribute access must raise a clear LazyParseError with source offset and chunk id for debugging
Performance strategy: minimize allocations; keep parse index as tuple list of (key, start, end) strings; reuse a shared buffer for repeated parses when safe
Compatibility: fallback to existing robust streaming parsers if binary encoder not available on platform
Docs: include code patterns for 'peek-first-field then decide to hydrate' and 'streaming aggregator that only materializes final embeddings'
progress_updates: 2026-03-01 - Ticket created; initial design sketch and goals captured. POC idea discussed in eng-api sync.
2026-03-03 - POC: implemented a minimal LazyStub using orjson loads on a single key; measured 28% first-field latency improvement on small prompt set (unoptimized)
2026-03-06 - Design review with SDK + Runtime teams. Decided on API flag 'response_schema_mode' and that .to_pydantic() will accept a timeout param for heavy hydration.

2026-03-10 - Benchmarked alternative parsers (rapidjson, simdjson). simdjson best for large payloads but requires native dependency; chose orjson as default with simdjson as opt-in on supported platforms.

2026-03-12 - Implemented checkpoint serialization for lazy stubs; verified deserialization across process boundary in test harness. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/4072

2026-03-14 - Running full perf suite; seeing 37% median improvement for first-field access on large model streams. Starting internal docs and examples for dev preview. Soliciting design + security review.
qa_notes: Add unit tests for single-key lazy access, nested field lazy access, and missing keys returning AttributeError-like semantics
Integration test: stream 10k items with mixed hydrating strategies ('lazy' consumers + 'eager' consumers) to validate memory isolation
Fuzz tests around chunk boundary splits and UTF-8 multi-byte splits in middle of tokens
Test retry scenarios with simulated transient socket failures and verify checkpoint resume behavior
